newsitem.title: USA: Thousands see Garth Brooks concert in New York.
newsitem.headline: Thousands see Garth Brooks concert in New York.

text.p: Hundreds of thousands of country music fans -- the wildly differing estimates ranged from 150,000 to one million -- whooped it up Thursday night at superstar Garth Brooks' free concert in Manhattan's Central Park.
"Hello, New York!" Brooks, whose record sales top Michael Jackson's and Elvis Presley's, screamed at the crowd when he came on stage around 8 p.m. EDT.
Blue and white spotlights swept over the standing-room-only crowd, which sang along to Brooks' opening numbers "Rodeo" and "Friends in Low Places."

Brooks told the audience that every conversation he had with reporters this week started out with the same question: "'Why New York City?' By God, this is why. New York City!" he said to the expansive, cheering crowd.

Singer and pianist Billy Joel, a native of Long Island, appeared on stage with Brooks, an Oklahoma native, to sing his hit "New York State of Mind." Songwriter Don McLean, whose hit "American Pie" of 1971 is occasionally performed by Brooks on tour, also joined the country singer for a duo version of that classic.

Some dedicated fans travelled into the city from out of state and camped out overnight to make certain they had good seats for the concert. Others just wandered in after work, more attracted by the spectacle of the crowd in cowboy hats and the prospect of visiting Central Park unmolested at night.

Estimates of the crowd ranged from 150,000 from the Parks Department, 250,000 from the New York City Police, 750,000 from promoters and even one million in some local news accounts. Only about one-tenth of the crowd could actually see the star in his trademark black hat. Most were content to see him on one of the five jumbo screens and many took pictures of the video image.

"Every once in a while we get a glimpse of him walking by, but only when we're jumping," said Marianne Barton, 27, who had driven eight hours from upstate New York to see the concert. "It would nice to see him, but I don't care. I'm just happy to be here."

New York City prepared for the concert, broadcast live on HBO, for days with traffic reporters warning of "Garthlock" and an inordinate number of people in cowboy hats walking the streets of Manhattan.
Brooks was the first country singer to perform in a major concert in Central Park. Other superstars who have performed in the park include Paul Simon, Elton John and Diana Ross.
